text:
Marta: Quick brainstorm 10m1 1: propose a maintenance-less cutover path for Private (VPC + on-prem) so customers who disallow windows can still upgrade. Deliverables: relay fallback pattern, egress-preserve installer flag, and a support runbook.

Raj: We need to be explicit about tradeoffs: maintenance-less = longer overall time, potential transient latencies, and reliance on relay which increases egress costs. Also clarify egress-preserve semantics (true no-IP-change vs best-effort).

Devon: Implementation sketch: 1) Pre-stage operator-shim on nodes with disabled rollout. 2) Start canary tenant routing through new shim + relay for control-plane operations. 3) Promote tenants in waves using DSCP or traffic-weighted routing, not changing SNAT unless customer opts-in. 4) After all tenants validated, flip active endpoints. Each promotion step has a rollback hook.

Samir: Field feedback: BankX and AcmeCorp require "no IP drift". For them we should offer an explicit "VIP handoff" option where customer sets up DNAT rules so control-plane stays on same egress IP. We'll need clear network pre-reqs doc for NetOps.

Elin: Technical constraints: VIP/DNAT path requires changes on the customer's L4 device and might fail in cloud environments with managed NAT gateways. Alternative is static SNAT provisioning which needs carrier support. We'll include both methods and map which customers are eligible.

Priya: Customer comms: two templates: "Maintenance Window" (fast path) and "Maintenance-less" (relay + staged promote). Call out estimated timelines: fast path <1h (including buffers); maintenance-less could be 6-48h depending on tenant count and traffic shaping. Explain residual risks and cost delta for relay.

Marta: Acceptance criteria idea: - No-downtime path completes without >1% error increase for 99% tenants. - Egress-preserve flag validated in staging with simulated NetOps rules. - Canary automation supports pause/resume and immediate rollback. - Runbook includes manual steps and verification commands.

Raj: Testing matrix: small state tenants (<=2GB) for fast path; large-state (>2GB) must be excluded from fast path and use staged transfer. Test topologies: NAT gateway, BGP, split-horizon DNS, IPv6 dual-stack, KMS rotation mid-upgrade. Add synthetic traffic replay to catch transient errors.

Devon: Rough effort: operator changes + routing automation = 10 dev-days, relay orchestration + billing knobs = 4 infra-days, QA matrix = 7 QA-days, docs + comms = 2 PD-days. Contingency: +30%.

Elin: Runbook snippet we'll include:\n```\n# preflight check\nkubectl -n redwood get cm operator-config -o yaml | grep egress-preserve\n# start canary wave\nredwoodctl upgrade start --wave canary --mode maintenance-less\n# verify metrics\npromql: increase(upgrades_failures_total[5m]) == 0\n```\n
Samir: Support asks: add a Console toggle per-tenant to enable relay fallback during the upgrade, and an event stream for egress-ip-change events. Support can flip relay if customer complains.

deploy-bot: nightly-ci: relay-orchestration branch tests passed (2026-03-22T05:10Z) :white_check_mark:

Marta: Action items: @Devon draft the maintenance-less spec and automation playbook; @Elin enumerate network pre-reqs and customer eligibility; @Priya prepare the two comms templates with cost/latency bullets; @Raj add the large-state perf tests to infra. Sync Friday 09:30 PT.

Raj: Also file Console story for the per-tenant toggle and upgrade metrics (upgrade_latency_seconds, egress_ip_change_total).

Marta: Thanks all 1: we want the spec + rough test harness by EOD Wednesday.
